doc.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Left-hand style and balance at the piano
summary: Bryant discusses his strong left hand and balance between hands.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: In listening to you play, especially on this most recent recording we’ll talk about along the way, I’m very impressed by the chording, the power of your left hand. It seems to me that you really like kind of chords in the two octaves below middle C, like kind of low sounding things, but they don’t sound muddy the way you play them. Is that something that you consider part of your style or is it just my imagination?

I guess so. I guess it would be a part of my style, yeah. I like to use the whole piano, but I try not to let one hand muddy up and destroy the other hand or something like that, try to get a balance in there. I figure that a piano is an instrument that you should be able to play alone. So and like I said the classical training helped in what I wanted to do with my left hand, as opposed to the right hand and so forth like that, and I guess it sort of evolved into some sort of a sound that was in my head that I had to get out of the piano. Through trial and error and so forth like that, the style evolved.
